title: Observation of universal hierarchical relaxation in a quantum simulator
authors: Jiaozi Wang, Manoj K. Joshi, Luca Capizzi, Rainer Blatt, Christian F. Roos, Leonardo Mazza, Dario Poletti
abstract: Autocorrelation functions play a key role in the theoretical characterization of the dynamical properties of interacting many-body quantum systems. Recently, bringing together the eigenstate thermalization hypothesis and hydrodynamics, it was theoretically predicted that the relaxation of autocorrelators can be described by the \textit{relaxation-overlap inequality}, which, when saturated, predicts a hierarchy of relaxation exponents for a set of operators that are easily identified and constructed. Here, we employ a trapped-ion quantum simulator to experimentally demonstrate it in the diffusive regime; to do so, we have extended the theory of the overlap-relaxation inequality to systems with multiple conservation laws. Our study thus opens the path to a thorough characterization of the relaxation to equilibrium and appearance of hydrodynamic behavior in quantum matter.
summary: This research uses a trapped-ion quantum simulator to experimentally verify the theoretical prediction of universal, hierarchical relaxation in interacting quantum systems. By measuring autocorrelation functions for operators of increasing complexity, the authors confirm that the relaxation decay rate is systematically governed by the operator's overlap order, extending fundamental concepts like the Eigenstate Thermalization Hypothesis to systems with multiple conserved quantities.
main_problem: The paper aims to experimentally characterize the dynamical properties and relaxation to equilibrium in interacting many-body quantum systems by demonstrating universal and hierarchical relaxation of autocorrelation functions.
main_result: The authors experimentally established the universal hierarchical relaxation regimes predicted by the saturated relaxation-overlap inequality, showing that the decay rate depends systematically on the spatial extent (overlap order) of the measured operators.
method: The study uses a trapped-ion quantum simulator to measure time-dependent autocorrelation functions of local observables, analyzing their algebraic decay rates.
model_or_system: The physical system is a one-dimensional chain of trapped $^{40}	ext{Ca}^+$ ions governed by a long-range XX Hamiltonian. The theory is extended to systems conserving multiple quantities, specifically energy and total magnetization.
key_observables:
Autocorrelation functions of local observables ($\langle \hat{O}(t) \hat{O}^\dagger angle_c$), relaxation exponents ($
u$), and overlap orders ($\mu$).
important_parameters:
Diffusive regime, multiple conserved charges (Energy and $\hat{S}_z$), and the overlap order $\mu$ which dictates the decay exponent ($
u \propto \mu/2$).
main_assumptions: The theory assumes the existence of a finite family of commuting conserved charges and postulates a generalized Eigenstate Thermalization Hypothesis (ETH) relation.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the ion trap setup, the hierarchy of autocorrelation function decays, and data collapses confirming the universal scaling behavior of the relaxation rates for different observables.
paper_structure: The paper builds from theoretical predictions (ROI extension to multiple charges) to experimental implementation on the trapped-ion simulator, measuring correlators for increasing operator complexity (overlap order $\mu$) to confirm the predicted hierarchical decay rates.
why_interesting: This work directly bridges advanced theoretical concepts (ROI, generalized ETH) with cutting-edge experimental capabilities (trapped ions) to probe fundamental non-equilibrium dynamics, which is highly relevant for understanding quantum thermalization.
